tasks.desc: Derive the reduced edge-bit parity model and the row/column xor-equation/DSU counting formula.
Implement the primary reduced parity union-find solution in Python and verify it on the sample plus small brute-force/random grids.
Finalize the code for performance and formatting: O(sum HW alpha(H+W)) time, O(H+W) memory per case, no hardcoded sample behavior, output one answer per test case.

proposals: Implement the reduced parity union-find solution as the primary method, streaming rows and maintaining column prefix parities.
Implement a full-edge parity union-find variant as a heavier independent sanity check on small cases.
Implement a generic sparse GF(2) rank checker on the reduced row/column equations for small random instances to verify consistency and component counts.
Implement a transfer-matrix DP for very small min(H,W) to cross-check the behavior on tiny tori.
Implement a brute-force enumerator for tiny grids to generate edge-case tests such as all A, all B, and dimensions equal to 2.
prev: Implement the primary reduced parity union-find solution in Python and verify it on the sample plus small brute-force/random grids: use fast tokenized input, an iterative parity DSU over H+W row/column nodes, maintain col_pref and row_pref, union row i with column W+j for each B cell with weight 1 ^ col_pref[j] ^ row_pref, update prefixes for A cells, check all row and column A counts are even and DSU consistency, and output pow(2, components, 998244353) or 0; provide the final code in the required delimiters.
